p|cli|trampa.ninguna: No traps placed. Place one with: guardiana trampa crear
p|cli|trampa.intacta: Nobody has asked for it yet.
p|cli|trampa.ya_hay: There is already a trap in that file: {archivo} [{id}]. Two in the same file do not work, because the second one covers the first. Remove the old one with: guardiana trampa quitar {id}
p|cli|trampa.sin_archivo: The file is gone: this trap cannot spring. Remove it with “guardiana trampa quitar {id}” or create it again.
p|cli|trampa.picada: TRIGGERED: times it was asked for: {n}. The first, on {fecha}, by {quien}.
p|cli|trampa.sin_programa: a program the system could not name
p|cli|apps.fin: Done. Queries with a known program: {n}.
p|cli|servicio.estado.stopped_motivo: Service: installed but stopped. The last time it tried to start, it said this: {motivo}
p|cli|servicio.estado.none: Service: not installed. GUARDIANA only works while this window is open.
p|cli|servicio.privilegios: Installing, removing or stopping the service needs administrator permission.
p|cli|servicio.no_soportado: The service only exists on Windows and macOS.
p|cli|servicio.dns_aviso: The service watches for real only if the system DNS points at GUARDIANA (option 3 or guardiana dns --apply --yes). Otherwise it only watches what it is asked.
p|cli|panel.sin_token: Cannot find the panel key at {ruta}. Is GUARDIANA running (service or option 1/3)?
p|cli|panel.sin_permiso: The panel key is kept by the service at {ruta} and only the administrator can read it. Type “sudo guardiana panel”: it gives you the link to open in your browser.
p|cli|panel.sin_permiso_windows: Windows will not let this user read the panel key ({ruta}). Open the Start menu, look for “GUARDIANA” and open it from there, or open “Command Prompt” with “Run as administrator” and type “guardiana panel”.
p|cli|panel.enlace_sudo: Open this link in your browser (it carries your session key; do not share it): {url}
p|cli|panel.esperando: GUARDIANA is starting. The panel opens by itself as soon as the service answers.
p|cli|comunicaciones.abriendo: Opening Communications in your browser. If it does not open, paste this link into it (it works once, for two minutes): {url}
p|cli|comunicaciones.ya_abierto: Communications was already open: bringing it to your browser. If it does not show, paste this link into it (it works once, for two minutes): {url}
p|cli|comunicaciones.cerrado: Communications closed: none of its pages was open in the browser any more.
p|cli|comunicaciones.sin_llave: This link no longer works. Open Communications from the applications menu (“GUARDIANA Communications”) or type guardiana comunicaciones in a terminal.
p|cli|comunicaciones.sin_sudo: Communications opens as your own user, without sudo: type guardiana comunicaciones. That way the keys of your conversations stay in your folder and your browser opens.
p|cli|comunicaciones.windows: On Windows, Communications is inside GUARDIANA ZERO: open it and go to its “Communications” tab.
p|cli|comunicaciones.sin_carpeta: I cannot find your home folder (the HOME variable is empty), so Communications has nowhere to keep your keys.
p|cli|comunicaciones.sin_carpeta_motivo: I could not prepare the Communications folder ({ruta}): {motivo}
p|cli|comunicaciones.sin_puerto: I could not open the local port of Communications on 127.0.0.1: {motivo}
p|cli|observe.puerto80: Could not open {addr} for the checker page ({motivo}). Phones can use http://{ip}:7443/mi-dispositivo.
p|cli|informe.fila: {nombre}: queries, {consultas}; to trackers, {rastreadores}; to advertising, {publicidad}; normal, {esperados}; blocked, {cortados}
p|cli|informe.total: Total: queries, {consultas}; to trackers, {rastreadores}; to advertising, {publicidad}; blocked, {cortados}
p|cli|reglas.cabecera: Rules (id, state, scope, type:pattern, action, device, created):
p|cli|reglas.ninguna: There are no rules. GUARDIANA only watches.
p|cli|reglas.deshecha: Rule undone. The record is kept.
p|cli|reglas.no_encontrada: There is no active rule with that number.
p|cli|reglas.numero_malo: “{id}” is not a rule number. The numbers are shown by “guardiana reglas”.
p|cli|verify.firma.dev: Signature: this program carries the DEVELOPMENT key, not the release key. There is no signature to check; it is not a released version.
p|cli|verify.firma.sin_archivo: Signature: not found. Download {archivo} from the install page into a folder and run verify from that folder: it checks the signature on your computer, without connecting to anything.
p|cli|verify.firma.sin_archivo_panel: Signature: the panel cannot check it, because the service does not see your downloads folder. Download {archivo} from the install page, open a terminal in that folder and type “guardiana verify”: it checks the signature on your computer, without connecting to anything.
p|cli|verify.firma.mac_zip: Signature: on a Mac what is published and signed is the .zip you downloaded, not the program inside it, so there is no signature to look for here. Check the .zip’s with minisign, as the install page explains.
p|cli|verify.registro.sin_archivo_panel: Public record: the panel cannot look up the hash, because the service does not see your downloads folder. Download ledger.jsonl from the install page, open a terminal in that folder and type “guardiana verify”.
p|cli|verify.firma.ok: Signature: correct. The program is signed with the GUARDIANA key it carries inside: {clave}. Compare it with the one published at guardianagroup.com/en/install.html.
p|cli|verify.firma.mal: Signature: does NOT match. The program or its signature has changed. Do not use it until this is cleared up.
p|cli|verify.registro.sin_archivo: Public record: there is no ledger.jsonl in this folder or next to the program. Download it from the install page into the same folder and run verify from there: it looks this hash up in the public record, on your computer.
p|cli|verify.registro.no_esta: Public record: this hash is NOT in ledger.jsonl. If this is a released version, something is off.
p|cli|verify.registro.ok: Public record: matches version {v} published on {fecha} (Rekor {rekor}).
p|cli|verify.dns.guardiana_primario: GUARDIANA changed the DNS: this computer’s queries go through it.
p|cli|verify.dns.guardiana_no_primario: GUARDIANA changed the DNS but RIGHT NOW the queries do not go through it: the system changed it back. The service reapplies it every minute; if it persists, use guardiana dns --apply --yes.
p|cli|verify.dns.guardiana_desconocido: GUARDIANA changed the DNS; could not check whether the queries go through it right now.
p|cli|verify.dns.sin_cambiar: GUARDIANA has not changed the system DNS.
p|cli|extracto.otra_clave: This ledger does not belong to this version of GUARDIANA: it was created by a version signed with a different key, and, for safety, the two are never mixed. If you are coming from a test version, move the ledger file elsewhere and GUARDIANA will start a new one. If you were not expecting this, delete nothing and write to hola@guardianagroup.com.
p|cli|verify.dns.solo_guardiana_sin_copi: System DNS: GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1) and nothing else. Every query from this computer goes through it.
p|cli|verify.dns.solo_guardiana_ajustes: System DNS: only GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1), according to the settings. Whether queries really arrive is what the check below says.
p|cli|verify.dns.apunta_sin_copia: This computer points at GUARDIANA, but GUARDIANA did not make that change: it has no record of the DNS you had before. On uninstall it will not be able to put it back exactly as it was. Apply it again from the panel so it is recorded.
p|cli|verify.vigilante: Guard Mode on for: {aparatos}. On those devices everything outside the declared scope is blocked, not only what the agent asks for.
p|cli|verify.hogar.aparcado: Home Mode: set aside, because the trial or the subscription ended. While GUARDIANA stands aside, port 53 stays open on the local network: it passes the home’s queries on, without looking at them or writing them down, so nobody is left without internet until you put the router’s DNS back.
p|cli|verify.puertos.ninguno: Ports open toward the local network: none.
p|cli|verify.puertos.abiertos: GUARDIANA ports open toward the local network: {puertos}.
p|cli|verify.puertos.no_leidos: Ports: could not read the system’s list of ports.
p|cli|verify.puertos.aviso: WARNING: Home Mode is off and there are GUARDIANA ports open toward the network. Wait a minute and check again; if it stays like this, tell us.
p|cli|verify.lista: List {id}: {n} entries, shipped inside the program; fetched on {fecha}.
p|cli|verify.cadena.mal: Ledger: the chain is BROKEN. See guardiana ledger --check.
p|cli|verify.extracto.sin_permiso: GUARDIANA may have changed the DNS, but this user cannot check it: only the administrator can read the ledger. Run it again with sudo (on Windows, “Run as administrator”).
p|cli|cli.extracto.sin_permiso: I cannot open this computer’s ledger: it belongs to the administrator. Run the command again with sudo (on Windows, “Run as administrator”).
p|cli|verify.cadena.sin_permiso: Ledger: it is there, but this user cannot read it. With sudo you get the event count and the chain check.
p|cli|observe.reconfigurando: Change in the home network or in Home Mode: GUARDIANA reopens its ports without stopping.
p|cli|observe.sin_arriba: The DNS of your network ({upstream}) has not answered for a minute. GUARDIANA gives this computer its DNS back as it was, so you keep your internet, and will ask again every minute.
p|cli|observe.vuelve_arriba: The DNS of your network answers again: GUARDIANA is this computer’s DNS once more.
p|cli|dns.estado.guardiana_primero: This computer’s queries go to GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1).
p|cli|dns.aplicado_panel: Done. This PC now goes through GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1). It used to resolve with: {originales}. It can be undone in “Status”.
p|cli|dns.consentimiento_si: To accept, repeat the command with --yes.
p|cli|dns.reserva_secundario: The resolver you have now stays as the secondary: if GUARDIANA stops, the computer keeps resolving through it.
p|cli|dns.solo_guardiana: On this computer GUARDIANA becomes the only resolver. That is what stops any query that goes through the system DNS slipping past it: systemd-resolved picks among the servers it has, it does not ask them in order, so leaving the old one as a second would mean part of the queries would never be seen. The service comes back by itself if it stops, and guardiana dns --restore puts everything back exactly as it was.
p|cli|dns.solo_guardiana_windows: On this computer GUARDIANA becomes the only DNS, over IPv6 too. That way no query that goes through the system DNS slips past it, and Edge does not go off to an encrypted DNS of its own. GUARDIANA keeps asking the servers you had, from the inside. If the service stops, the computer gets its previous DNS back until it starts again, and uninstalling leaves it exactly as it was.
p|cli|dns.solo_guardiana_mac: On this Mac GUARDIANA becomes the only DNS. That way no query that goes through the system DNS slips past it, and Chrome or Edge do not go off on their own to an encrypted DNS. GUARDIANA keeps asking the network’s servers behind the scenes. If the service stops, the Mac gets its previous DNS back until it starts again, and uninstalling leaves it exactly as it was.
p|cli|dns.camino_ok: Checked: a query made by Windows just now reached GUARDIANA.
p|cli|dns.camino_no: WARNING: a query made by Windows just now did NOT reach GUARDIANA, so you will not see anything yet. Disconnect the Wi‑Fi and connect it again (or restart) and check again in “Verify”. If it stays like this, write to hola@guardianagroup.com.
p|cli|dns.guardiana_no_contesta: Nothing changed: GUARDIANA is not answering on 127.0.0.1, and pointing this computer there would leave it without internet. Start the service (guardiana service start) and run the command again.
p|cli|dns.camino_no_deshecho: A query made just now by this computer did NOT reach GUARDIANA, so the DNS was put back exactly as it was and nothing changed. Disconnect the Wi‑Fi and connect it again (or restart) and run the command again. If it stays like this, write to hola@guardianagroup.com.
p|cli|verify.dns.guardiana_con_reserva: System DNS: GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1), with {dns} as the fallback. If GUARDIANA stops, the computer asks the fallback and those queries are not written down.
p|cli|verify.dns.por_guardiana: System DNS: GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1), which forwards to {dns}.
p|cli|verify.dns.camino_ok: Real test: a query made by the system just now reached GUARDIANA.
p|cli|verify.dns.camino_no: Real test: a query made by the system just now did NOT reach GUARDIANA.
p|cli|observe.caducado: The trial is over and there is no active license. GUARDIANA does not switch off: it keeps watching this computer on GUARDIANA Free, with the DNS as it was. What was written down is whole on your disk. To get everything in Plus back, activate your key in the panel.
p|cli|observe.caducado_plus: The subscription has ended. GUARDIANA does not switch off: it keeps watching this computer on GUARDIANA Free, with the DNS as it was. What was written down is whole on your disk. To get everything in Plus back, activate your key in the panel.
p|cli|verify.dns.camino_no.parado: The GUARDIANA service is stopped and the settings still point at it, so nothing answers: start the service (guardiana service start) or give back the previous DNS with guardiana dns --restore.
p|cli|verify.dns.camino_no.sin_servicio: GUARDIANA is not installed as a service and the settings still point at it, so nothing answers: give back the previous DNS with guardiana dns --restore.
p|cli|verify.dns.camino_no.ajustes: The settings point at GUARDIANA but the system resolves another way. Disconnect the network and connect it again, or restart; if it stays like this, write to us.
p|cli|verify.dns.guardiana_apunta: The DNS settings point at GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1).
p|cli|verify.dns.guardiana_no_primario_p: The service is stopped and, as it always does when it stops, it gave this computer its previous DNS back. It keeps the copy: when it starts, it steps in front again.
p|cli|verify.dns.guardiana_apartada: GUARDIANA stepped aside on its own because your network’s DNS is not answering, so you are not left without internet. It comes back by itself as soon as it answers.
p|cli|verify.registro.mac_sin_archivo: Public record: there is no ledger.jsonl on this computer. On a Mac the public record lists the .zip you downloaded, not the program inside it: compare that .zip’s hash with the one on the website.
p|cli|verify.registro.mac_zip: Public record: on a Mac the public record lists the .zip you downloaded, not the program inside it, so this hash cannot be in it. Compare the .zip’s hash with the one on the website.
p|cli|verify.registro.mac_zip_huella: Public record: on a Mac the public record lists the .zip, not the program inside it. This version’s is {archivo}, hash {sha}: compare it with the .zip you downloaded.
p|cli|verify.puertos.de_otros: Other programs hold these ports open toward the local network; they are not GUARDIANA’s: {puertos}.
p|cli|verify.puertos.dueno_desconocido: These ports are open toward the local network by a program the system will not name without administrator rights: {puertos}. They are not put down to GUARDIANA; to see whose they are, run verify again as administrator.
p|cli|observe.hogar_puerto_ocupado: Home Mode: {addr} could not be opened for the home’s devices (another program holds it or the address changed). This computer is still watched; it is tried again at the next check.
p|cli|observe.resolutor_caido: The resolver stopped answering on its own; GUARDIANA brings it back up.
p|cli|panel.tarda: This is taking longer than usual. If it does not open within a minute, open the Start menu, look for “GUARDIANA” and open it from there.
p|cli|panel.abriendo_espera: GUARDIANA is starting: the browser opens the panel as soon as it answers.
